author: Robert Carr
description: Tender chicken thighs gently simmered with browned mushrooms, white beans, tomatoes, spinach, and basil in a garlic-balsamic sauce.
equipment: Wide 4- to 5-quart stainless steel saute pan with a lid, such as All-Clad D5, or a Dutch oven
Knife and separate cutting boards for produce and raw chicken
Plate for partially cooked chicken; clean serving utensils
Shallow refrigerator- and freezer-safe containers, for meal prep
Food processor with 4 mm slicing disc and chopping blade, optional for vegetables

groceryIngredients.note: Plain, unbrined; trim visible fat. About 680 g after trimming.
No-salt-added, 15 oz cans; drain and rinse. About 3 cups drained beans total.
No-salt-added, 28 oz can; include the juices.
Ordinary balsamic vinegar, not sweetened glaze; 2 tbsp simmering and 1 tbsp finish.
Fine table salt; 1/4 tsp chicken and 1/4 tsp sauce. Do not substitute coarse salt by volume.
Lightly packed leaves, torn just before adding.

ingredients: 1 1/2 lb (680 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs after trimming visible fat, plain and unbrined
2 cans (15 oz each) no-salt-added cannellini beans, drained and rinsed, about 3 cups total
1 can (28 oz) no-salt-added diced tomatoes, with juices
3 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, divided; not balsamic glaze
1/2 teaspoon fine table salt, divided: 1/4 teaspoon chicken and 1/4 teaspoon sauce
1/4 cup lightly packed fresh basil leaves, torn
Water, only as needed to loosen the sauce
instructions: Prepare the washed produce and drain and rinse the beans. Pat the chicken dry; do not rinse it. Trim visible fat, unfold the thighs, and season with 1/4 teaspoon salt and the black pepper. For stainless steel, preheat a wide 4- to 5-quart saute pan over medium heat, then add 1 tablespoon oil for a single batch, or 1 1/2 teaspoons per batch if two batches are needed. For a Dutch oven, heat that same measured oil with the pot over medium heat. When the oil shimmers without smoking, lay the chicken in one layer and brown for about 3 minutes per side, allowing the first side to release before turning and lowering heat if the pan residue darkens too fast; it need not be cooked through yet. Work in batches if crowded, dividing the tablespoon of oil between batches. Transfer to a plate reserved for partially cooked chicken, and continue cooking immediately. Wash hands and clean raw-chicken preparation surfaces.

Use medium to medium-low heat and add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil, mushrooms, onion, and remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt. Cook for 7 to 9 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms lose their water and start to brown and the onion softens. Scrape up browned, not burned, bits; add a tablespoon of water if the pan threatens to scorch.

Add the garlic, tomato paste, oregano, and optional red pepper. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant and the paste darkens slightly. Stir in 2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, scraping the pan, then add the tomatoes with their juices and the drained beans. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Nestle the chicken and any accumulated juices into the sauce. Partially cover and simmer gently for about 12 to 18 minutes, turning the thighs halfway through, until every piece is at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C) in its thickest part. Thighs can be taken to about 175 degrees F for a more tender texture. Keep it at a gentle simmer rather than a hard boil; add a small splash of water only if the sauce becomes too thick. Use clean utensils for the finished chicken.

Transfer the cooked chicken to a clean plate briefly. Fold spinach into the sauce in handfuls and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted. If the sauce looks watery, simmer it uncovered a few minutes with the chicken out; if too thick, add water a tablespoon at a time. Remove from heat, stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon balsamic vinegar and the basil, then return the chicken to the sauce.

Divide the chicken, beans, vegetables, and sauce equally among four bowls. This is a complete bean-and-vegetable dinner without a required rice side. Serve promptly or portion into shallow containers and begin chilling. Keep chicken covered with some sauce in each meal-prep portion.
notes: Allow about 50 minutes overall and 20 to 25 minutes of hands-on work; allow another 5 to 10 minutes if the chicken needs two searing batches. Use a wide pan with at least 4 quarts capacity, not a small shallow skillet or a 3-quart saute pan. With stainless steel, including All-Clad D5, use moderate heat rather than maximum heat or induction boost, dry the chicken, and wait for it to release before turning. Keep browned pan residue for deglazing, but cool the pan enough to clean out blackened residue safely. Brown mushrooms and tomato paste before adding liquid; these steps provide depth without bouillon, cream, or cheese. The measured balsamic is vinegar, not a sweet glaze.

Trim the thighs well and use no-salt-added beans, tomatoes, and tomato paste. Fine table salt and oil are measured for the full meal. Boneless skinless chicken breast can replace thighs by weight: cut into even 3/4-inch-thick portions, brown briefly, then begin checking after 5 minutes in the simmering sauce and remove at 165 degrees F rather than using the thigh tenderness target. Return only to coat in the finished sauce.

Meal prep: Divide cooked food promptly among shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours, or within 1 hour above 90 degrees F. Keep the refrigerator at 40 degrees F or below. Use refrigerated portions within 3 to 4 days; freeze later portions promptly after chilling rather than waiting until the end of that window. Label and freeze at 0 degrees F or below, aiming to use within 2 months for quality. Do not cool a large batch on the counter.

Reheating: Thaw one frozen portion overnight in the refrigerator. Add 1 to 2 tablespoons water, cover with a microwave-safe vented lid, and heat at medium to medium-high power in 60-second intervals, stirring or turning between intervals. Use shorter intervals near the end. After a 1-minute stand, check several spots with a thermometer and continue until all hot components reach 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Reheat only the portion being eaten and serve promptly. Keep some tomato-bean sauce over the chicken while heating. Alternatively, warm gently in a covered saucepan, stirring and checking for 165 degrees F throughout. Add a few fresh basil leaves after reheating when available.

For Sunday preparation, refrigerate the portions intended for the next 3 days and freeze the later ones after chilling. Beans and tomato sauce freeze well for this style of meal; spinach will become softer. Thaw in the refrigerator, not on the counter.

Frozen spinach can replace the fresh spinach: use 1/2 cup thawed and squeezed plain chopped spinach, cook according to its package, and stir into the sauce near the end until hot. Plain frozen sliced mushrooms also work by weight, but cook off their extra moisture before adding tomato paste. Do not add sauces or extra salt to compensate for frozen vegetables.

For eight meals, use two pans or a larger pot with batch browning and allow extra time. Great Northern beans can replace cannellini beans in the same drained amount. Neither an additional starch side nor a cheese garnish is needed; keep optional additions separate from the base grocery quantities.

Optional Cuisinart DFP-14BCNY prep: Use the supplied 4 mm slicing disc for the trimmed mushrooms, feeding with the pusher and light pressure. Use the chopping blade to pulse the onion, first cut into 1-inch pieces, until finely chopped but not pureed; chop garlic separately because it enters the pan later. Keep within the manual's 3-cup capacity for chopped vegetables, even though the bowl holds 14 cups of sliced vegetables. Stop and unplug before changing blades or scraping, and keep hands out of the feed tube. Keep mushrooms sliced rather than finely minced, tear basil by hand, and leave the beans and finished sauce chunky. Process produce before handling raw chicken; the processor is a shortcut, not required equipment.
title: Tomato-Balsamic Chicken with White Beans and Spinach
